newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed down on Thursday on profit-taking after rising steadily for six days, brokers said.
The all share closed 10.2 points down at 796 after rising 35.2 points or 4.6 percent to 806.2 between June 16 and Wednesday, they said.
Price declines outnumbered gains by 60 to 18, as retail investors took profit across a wide range of stocks.
"Profit-taking would probably continue but the all share should not fall below about 775 points," said Subram Ramaswamy of Bartleet Mallory Stock Brokers.
Turnover, led by foreign buying of 100,000 shares each of Development Finance Corporation and National Development Bank, was 132.6 million rupees.
Foreign buying was worth 88.5 million rupees and selling was worth 26.5 million rupees.
"The index is likely to remain flat after profit-taking until corporate profits for the period ended June 1997 become known in early July," said a broker who declined to be identified.
"The profits to June which are expected to be good should spur the next upward movement, which should take the index to about 850 points," he added. --- Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319
